chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Harith ibn Muhammad, from Burayd al-Ajli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had relations with his wife on a day he is making up from the month of Ramadan, he said: If he had relations with his wife before midday (zuwal), there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day; and if he had relations with his wife after midday, then upon him is to give charity to ten poor people.

key_terms.يَوْمٍ يَقْضِيهِ: a day to be made up (qada)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation for breaking the fast in Ramadan before or after midday?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar establishes the principle of *ta'khir* (delay) in expiation, distinguishing between minor and major breaches based on the time of *zuwal* (noon). It reflects the Shia juristic view that the severity of the sin escalates if the act occurs after the sun has passed its zenith, requiring both *kaffarah* (feeding ten poor) and *qada* (making up the day). This ruling underscores the importance of timing in ritual purity and obligation within Shia fiqh.
